title: How do training zones and zone models work?
seoTitle: Training Zones and Zone Models in augo | augo support
description: augo ships seven zone models across run, bike and swim, and coaches can build their own. Zones are percentages of a performance anchor.
summary: A zone model defines training zones as percentages of a performance anchor — threshold pace, FTP, lactate threshold heart rate or critical power. augo ships seven models across run, bike and swim, and you can build your own or customise one for a single athlete.

body.html: A zone model turns one baseline number into a set of training zones. The zones are defined as percentages of a performance anchor, so when the athlete’s threshold moves, every zone moves with it.

The models augo ships

  • Run — heart rate 5-zone, heart rate 7-zone, pace 7-zone
  • Bike — heart rate 5-zone, heart rate 7-zone, power 6-zone
  • Swim — pace 5-zone

Zones are labelled in the usual language — Recovery, Endurance, Tempo, Threshold, VO2 Max, Anaerobic capacity — with the 7-zone models splitting threshold into sub- and super-threshold. The top zone is open-ended.

The four anchor types

Every model is built on one of four anchors:

  • Threshold pace
  • Lactate threshold heart rate
  • Functional threshold power (FTP)
  • Critical power

Which one you use is a coaching decision. augo doesn’t impose a methodology.

Building your own

You can create your own models with your own zone count, labels, colours and percentage bounds — and you can customise a model for a single athlete when someone doesn’t fit your standard template. Models you don’t use can be hidden so your catalogue stays short.

faqs.question: Which zone models does augo provide?
faqs.answer: Seven: run heart-rate 5 and 7 zone, run pace 7 zone, bike heart-rate 5 and 7 zone, bike power 6 zone, and swim pace 5 zone. You can also build your own.

faqs.question: Can I customise zones for one athlete?
faqs.answer: Yes. A model can be customised for a single athlete without changing the version other athletes are on.

faqs.question: What are zones based on?
faqs.answer: Percentages of a performance anchor — threshold pace, lactate threshold heart rate, FTP or critical power.
